Community benchmarks from
[RConsortium/pharma-skills](https://github.com/RConsortium/pharma-skills)
(R Consortium Submissions Working Group, Pilot 7). Each benchmark issue runs
the same task **with** and **without** the skill and scores both against a
rubric written by the issue author.

::: {.callout-note}
This is an informal snapshot compiled from the public issues on
November 5, 2026. It is not an official R Consortium summary. Several figures
were read from long comment threads, so check the linked issue before quoting
a number.
:::

## By skill

Mean % of rubric items passed, using the latest scored run per issue (mostly
Claude models). W / T / L = skill wins, ties, losses.

| Skill | With skill | Without | W / T / L |
|:--|--:|--:|:-:|
| admiral-adsl | **93%** | 70% | 2 / 1 / 0 |
| admiral-adae | **100%** | 67% | 2 / 0 / 0 |
| admiral-bds | **91%** | 72% | 3 / 0 / 0 |
| admiral-adtte, admiral-adrs | **82%** | 56% | 2 / 0 / 0 |
| sdtm-oak | **88%** | 63% | 1 / 0 / 0 |
| group-sequential-design | **73%** | 51% | 10 / 2 / 3 |
| clinical-trial-simulation | 90% | **91%** | 0 / 1 / 1 |

**Pattern:** large gains on convention-heavy ADaM and SDTM derivations; little
or no gain where the base model already knows the method.

**group-sequential-design** has its own roll-ups across 15–21 trial-design
scenarios:

- [#80](https://github.com/RConsortium/pharma-skills/issues/80): latest run per
  issue (April 28): **73%** vs 51%; 10 wins, 2 ties, 3 losses.
- [#146](https://github.com/RConsortium/pharma-skills/issues/146): best
  with-skill run per issue (May 31): **90%** vs 62%; 16 wins, 4 ties, 1 loss.
  This picks the skill's best showing, so treat it as a ceiling.

## Caveats

- Small numbers of runs; rubrics differ by issue and several were tightened
  and re-scored over time.
- Runs vary in model, skill version, and date. Results are directional, not a
  validated comparison.
- Losses for group-sequential-design were mostly scope gaps (problems outside
  what the skill covers), not the base model being better.
